question: Is specimen-to-specimen variation of single-cell program scores better described by re-weighting shared components (prevalence) or by shifting one shape (intensity), across programs, representations and cohorts; how stable is the frozen representation across training runs; what patient and cell numbers would a prognostic study need?

stability.match: Hungarian on Pearson correlation of sqrt(beta)

stage_gate.stage_b_requires: reviewed Stage-A contracts plus user approval

not_claims: A better held-out likelihood for re-weighting is a statistical description, not proof of discrete biological states.
External cohorts without authoritative outcomes remain construct evaluations, not prognostic validation.
The design calculator gives conditional planning numbers, not a clinically justified effect size.
